about: Labelled pictures for the next screenshot reading measurement (plan 103, lane P1). Same shape as screenshot_eval_v0.json (v0 stays), plus the fields below. 'file' is a name inside the workshop's screenshots/plan103-set folder (give it to the script with --root); each file is the picture shrunk the way the plugin's Low attachment setting does it (longest side 800, JPEG quality 62). 'source' is where the full-size original sits, under the workshop's screenshots folder. New fields: 'game_named_on_screen' (false when the picture never writes the game's name, so a right answer has to come from what the game looks like); 'place' and 'place_aliases' (an area name, empty when none is legible or certain); 'expect_section' (the name of the library note whose subject is on screen, empty when there is none; 'expect_section_also' lists notes that also fit) - the test in tests/test_screenshot_eval_v1_labels.py checks every one names a real note; 'in_library' (false when the library holds no notes for the game, and its app_id is then only the Deck's own id); 'confidence' (how sure the labeller is of each label: high, medium, low, or none when the label is empty). 'boss' is the boss or named enemy on screen, empty when none; a boss with confidence 'low' is a guess. Pictures were chosen from what the Deck held on 2026-11-09: game screens only, near-duplicates dropped, the performance overlay and Steam's 'Screenshot Taken' pop-up left in where they were. Added on 2026-11-11 (plan 103 follow-up, lane P5): 23 public boss and enemy pictures, files named p5-<game>-<boss>-<n>, whose 'source' is under the workshop's screenshots/plan103-boss-candidates/originals folder and whose 'file' is the 800-pixel copy made there (longest side 800, JPEG quality 62). The new field 'origin' says where such a picture came from (its page address) and that it is a public screenshot approved by the maintainer on 2026-11-11, for a private test only; the older pictures were taken on the Deck and have no 'origin'. For the emulated games (Paper Mario, Pikmin 2, Super Mario 64, Yoshi's Story) the Deck's own shortcut number is not known here, so 'app_id' carries the library's own name for the game and the notes search finds the game by its name. A 'place' is only set where the library note or the wiki page names it and the picture agrees; a picture's 'note' says where the labeller was not sure.
